subject.title: Memory MVP: build write pipeline with classification, dedupe, merge, and conflict handling

question: Should the Memory MVP write resolver become a first-class memory-core SQLite capability now, or should OpenClaw keep the current Markdown/dreaming/wiki layers until a narrower schema and plugin-API plan is sponsored?
rationale: The issue is valid but crosses durable data model, plugin ownership, provenance, conflict review, and operator UX decisions that source inspection cannot safely choose automatically.

options.title: Sponsor a memory-core MVP design
options.body: Define the typed SQLite record model, source/provenance contract, resolver decisions, and review queue before implementation begins.

options.title: Defer to existing layers
options.body: Keep Markdown memory, dreaming promotion, and memory-wiki as the supported path for now and close or retarget this later if maintainers decide not to add a resolver.

options.title: Expose plugin API first
options.body: Add only the missing plugin seams so an external memory plugin can own durable writes without expanding core memory-core behavior.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a memory-core MVP design
recommendation.body: Define the typed SQLite record model, source/provenance contract, resolver decisions, and review queue before implementation begins.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work touches both memory-core and memory-wiki, and the decision needs someone familiar with the current memory stack boundaries.
